area: World, Style (the scale of the scenery)
question: Real-world heights for trees, houses and walls (prototype px today: walls 5-7 m, houses 10.7-14.5 m, trees 6-29 m at 2 px/m)? Alex: '12 yes, but show me'.
source: scripts/ui/boards/scenery_heights_board_shot.gd: one run of the real game per option and map (BoardScene on the Strike, seed 20261009, and Hold the bridge, seed 55; fog off, labels off, the sun fixed at 315 / 46), the heights switched by scripts/ui/boards/scenery_heights_patch.gd. Rendered in a throwaway checkout at HEAD because other builders were editing the units' data in the shared tree.

held_constant.sun: FIXED (data/params/sun.json mode 'fixed': bearing 315, elevation 46, a shadow 0.966 x the height) so the frames compare; the game's live sun follows the time of day (0.58 x at noon to 2.0 x), which makes every difference between options larger
held_constant.map: the same map, water, fog off; the same crowns, footprints, tree placement and random streams in every option (a height is read by the shadow passes only): the measured square holds the same 2361 trees on the Strike and 2813 on seed 55 in all four options
held_constant.units: a tank on the village road (Strike), a light fighter in the low band (120 m) over the village's south edge, the Strike's own tower and bridge; on seed 55 the two player tanks and the bridge (the enemy tanks and the cruiser are out of the shot); every other unit waits at (4400, 4400)
held_constant.left_off: the HUD, the height and speed lettering, the target ring, the roster
held_constant.zooms: planning zoom 0.35 (0.7 px per metre) and the closest zoom 3.0 (6 px per metre), the same camera centres in every option

mechanism.what: Heights are set by three lines of the port: scene_gen.gd sync_tree (t.h = t.r * P.height * (0.85 + 0.3 * t.hr)), structures.gd sync_struct (s.h = P.wallH * s.hs for a wall, P.houseSize * 0.9 * s.hs for a house) and village_draw.gd (a hedge tree's h = r * P.height * (...) * terrain.json hedge.height_frac). A height drives the shadow passes (terrain_shadows.gd, chunk_terrain_provider.gd _struct_sil) and the trees' draw order, and nothing else: sprites, footprints, crowns, tree placement and every random draw are independent of it.
mechanism.board_override: scripts/ui/boards/scenery_heights_patch.gd rewrites the two lines of scene_gen.gd and structures.gd in memory (Script.source_code + reload(), before the first instance; the files on disk are untouched) and puts the option's numbers in Engine meta 'scenery_heights'. With no meta the patched lines compute what they computed before. The hedge trees are not patched: they are already about 2 m.
mechanism.why_not_data: wall_height and tree_height are data keys; a house's height is the literal 0.9 x house_size (the footprint's own scale, so house_size cannot be used), and trees have no height window.

to_make_it_live._about: PROPOSED, if Alex picks an option: each option's own 'to_make_it_live' lists the values. Data edits alone: parameters.wall_height.default and parameters.tree_height.default (plus a prototype_default beside each). Two small code edits: a house_height_ratio key replacing the literal 0.9 in structures.gd sync_struct (default 0.9 keeps the port check), and a tree_height_min_m / tree_height_max_m window in scene_gen.gd sync_tree (absent = no clamp, which the port check needs). RenderParams reads both (render_params.gd); test_scene_gen, test_port_utils and --parity keep the prototype's values through prototype_default. The board's patch file and this board script are then retired or kept as a look-compare tool.

subjects.title: The village: the radio tower, its walled compound, houses and a tank
A wood's edge, a hedged field and open ground
A plane at 120 m (low band) over houses and a wood, for scale
The bridge on seed 55 with a tank beside it

notes_proposed: WHAT CHANGES IN THE SHADOWS. Houses and walls carry the change; trees hardly move. At the board's sun a house's shadow goes from 12.0 m to 6.7 m in S1 (at the game's longest sun, x2.0, from 24.9 m to 13.8 m): today it is as long as the house is deep and falls across the next house and the road, in S1 it is a short wedge. The compound's rampart ring throws a 5.8 m shadow today (a second ring beside the 8 m wide earthwork) and 2.4 m in S1, so it reads as a low earthwork with a thin shadow instead of a fortress wall: the outer wall is 2.4 to 3.0 tanks tall today and 1.0 to 1.3 in S1, a house 5.0 to 6.2 tanks today and 2.8 to 3.5 in S1. The radio tower, unchanged at 23 to 27 m, goes from twice a house's height to 3.6 times it.

TREES. S1 changes a tree's shadow by little: the median tree goes from 11.2 m to 12.3 m, its shadow from 10.8 m to 11.9 m, and only the tails move (the 1.4 percent of trees over 20 m, up to 28.7 m, stop at 20; the smallest, under 7.3 m today, come up to 8 m). Today's trees are already real-sized: the median is 11.2 m on this map (the 12.7 m of the study was the theoretical middle), a plausible broadleaf. What is odd today is that a median tree is SHORTER than a house (0.9 x); in S1 it is 1.8 x. S3's trees are 30 percent taller than today's: 74 percent of them reach the 12 m terrain step and 13.5 percent pass 20 m.

AT THE PLANNING ZOOM the four options are close to indistinguishable: a house's shadow is 8 px long at 0.7 px per metre today and 5 px in S1, and the walls' and trees' differences are 1 to 3 px (compare the first row of each subject). The choice is plain at the closest zoom 3.0, where a house's shadow is 72 px today and 40 px in S1 beside a tank 54 px long. It is a close-up decision, and the game's longer sun (x2.0) doubles every difference.

THE REASON FOR S3, CHECKED. A crown is drawn 19 m across (the prototype's 38 px at 2 px/m), and a tree's shadow is displaced by its height times the sun's length: 7.7 m (15.5 px) for a tree of 8 m against a crown radius of about 19 px, so only the shortest trees' shadows start to hide under their own crowns, and S1's floor of 8 m already holds those. In the planning rows S1 and S3 are hard to tell apart; S3's extra height buys little and costs a tree shadow twice as long as a house's (14.1 m against 6.7 m) and three quarters of the trees as tall as the terrain step.

THE HEDGES AND THE PLANE. Hedge trees are already 1.3 to 4.2 m (median 2.4 m, about a tank's height) in all four, so no option touches them and S1's 'hedges about 2 m' is met. A low-band plane's shadow stands 1.2 m from it in every option (the decided 1 percent rule), unrelated to the scenery's heights.

WHAT TO DECIDE (Alex), one recommendation each, all PROPOSED. (1) Houses and walls to real heights? Recommended yes, S1's numbers: a house 0.5 x its footprint scale (about 7 m to the ridge) and walls 5 px (2.5 m). (2) Trees: lift 10 percent and hold to 8 to 20 m (S1), or leave them as they are? Recommended S1's rule, but it is the one part with no visible difference at the planning zoom and it needs a new height window in the tree generator; leaving tree_height at 1.3 is a defensible smaller change. (3) Keep S2 (halfway) or S3 (taller trees) in play? Recommended no: S2 is a compromise nobody asked for and S3's reason is met by S1's 8 m floor.

WHAT IT COSTS TO MAKE LIVE (PROPOSED). Data: wall_height 12 to 5, with a prototype_default of 12 beside it (so --parity and test_scene_gen still compare with the prototype, as shadow_strength does). One new key, house_height_ratio, replacing the literal 0.9 in structures.gd (0.9 to 0.5; default 0.9 keeps the port check). If the tree rule is taken, a tree_height_min_m / tree_height_max_m window in scene_gen.gd sync_tree (absent means no clamp). terrain.json's 'tallest tree (~14 m)' text reworded (24 m + 20 m = 44 m stays under the 120 m low band, Track S's constraint). No sprite, footprint or random stream changes, so every map bakes as before apart from the shadow passes. One caution: wall_height and the house ratio are in prototype px, right only at the demo baseline of 2 px per metre; a key in metres times px_per_m would follow the map-scale knob.
recommendation_proposed: S1 (PROPOSED, Alex decides): houses about 7 m to the ridge, compound walls about 2.5 m, trees held to 8 to 20 m (median 12.3). It fixes the two clear misfits (a house 5 to 6 tanks high, a wall 2.4 to 3 tanks) and puts the tower, trees, houses, walls and tanks in the real order of heights (25 m, 12 m, 7 m, 2.5 m, 2.3 m), while the trees themselves hardly change. If Alex wants the smallest edit: S1's houses and walls with today's trees, two data values and one new key, which looks the same at the planning zoom. Not S3 (its reason is met by S1's 8 m floor) and not S2 (a compromise nobody asked for).
palette_check: Heights add no colour: every shadow is the one steel tint at the same strength, a shadow over a lit roof the roof-shaded chip. Taller scenery puts more of the ground in shadow (the mean lightness of the closest-zoom frames is in each option), a change in the SHARE of the ground in shadow, not in the lightness ramp. The chart's bars use the object, roof, wall and rock fills. Material stays linework: sprites and the shadow-side pen are identical in every option.
